title: Quantifying Spatial Under-reporting Disparities in Resident Crowdsourcing
authors: Zhi Liu, Uma Bhandaram, Nikhil Garg
source_version: Nature Computational Science 4, 57-65 (2024); version of record published 2023-12-05; DOI 10.1038/s43588-023-00572-6
last_status_checkpoint: 2026-06-28: public partial checkpoint after tightening the finite observed-window proof campaign to a primitive wrapper boundary. Theorem 1 / Appendix Theorem 2 now have preferred rows through `Theorem2PrimitiveSourceModel`, which packages a homogeneous Poisson count-process law together with fixed paper `g(s)` and `h_m(e)` kernels; Lean derives the rate-indexed Condition 1/2 semantics, source-data factorizations, finite independent Poisson count-family witnesses, and collapsed total-PMF likelihood route from that wrapper. The Eq. (33)/(34) min-censored preprocessing rules produce `StoppingObservationWindow` records from explicit endpoint stopping-time premises, deterministic endpoint specializations, first-count-arrival certificates, and a single `DurationCensoredFirstCountObservationCertificate`; Lean also derives pathwise deterministic observation-window projections and zero/one/multi-report Appendix B.2 factorization over the certified pathwise exposure. Remaining boundary: supply/prove the standard homogeneous Poisson counting-process law and the duration-censored stopping certificate fields for the concrete process/endpoints, plus fixed paper Condition 1/2 kernels.
main_caveat: The Poisson count algebra, Lemma 1 continuous-duration observed-rate formula and probability bounds, finite-duration weighted-average detection-probability identity, continuous-duration Poisson thinning count law, IID unit-interval LLN route to the continuous observed rate, exponential reporting-delay mean, Appendix B.2 zero/one/multi-report source-case algebra, condition-function and observed-jump-time source-data constructors including ordered-window jump-time rows, explicit no-arrival/interarrival process-kernel collection, finite-product likelihood kernels, full Poisson-binomial thinning algebra, Lemma 2 restricted-start tail, memoryless-ratio, PMF-mass, density-mixture bridges, one/finite-jump process-law normalization, ordered-region volume normalization, generic arrival-kernel case factorization, Eq. (33)/(34) min-censored stopping-window construction from endpoint stopping-time premises, deterministic endpoint specializations, first-count-arrival certificate variants, duration-censored local stopping certificate route including stochastic endpoint, pathwise deterministic-window projections, and zero/one/multi-report source-data factorization over certified pathwise windows, fixed-function Condition 1/2 density-source route, non-identifiability collisions including positive-premise variants, MLE score/global log-likelihood optimality, Poisson-regression likelihood, and zero-inflated likelihood rows are Lean-checked. The preferred finite Theorem 1 / Appendix Theorem 2 rows now route through `Theorem2PrimitiveSourceModel`: fixed `g(s)` and `h_m(e)` data build the rate-indexed source model with rate-independence proved by reflexivity, and the homogeneous count-process law drives the Poisson PMF consequences plus constructed `FinitePoissonCountFamily` witnesses. The legacy source bundle `assumption_theorem2_poisson_process_and_conditions` remains an audit layer. Future reusable-library work is narrowed to proving/supplying the homogeneous Poisson counting-process law and the duration-censored stopping certificate fields for the concrete process/endpoints, together with fixed paper Condition 1/2 kernels.
human_summary: Poisson likelihood algebra, Lemma 1/2 consequences, MLE/regression/zero-inflation rows, and the Eq. (33)/(34) stopping-window bridge compile; full formalization requires a compact homogeneous Poisson process, stopping-certificate, and fixed-kernel certificate bundle.

paper_interface.maintainability_issue: Review surface has 84 paper-interface rows, above the 30-row LLM audit threshold and below the 120-row curation threshold; broad theorem wrappers are retained as auxiliary proof-facing rows; closeout sidecars are current for this public partial checkpoint.

llm_statement_review.policy: Translate each Lean statement with an LLM that has no paper context and require it to preserve every visible binder, hypothesis, domain condition, equivalence direction, and conclusion. Have a third LLM compare that TeX/prose translation with the original full paper statement, not just the theorem label. A `matches` verdict requires equivalence of hypotheses, subparts, quantifiers, domains, constants, normalizations, signs, inequality directions, and conclusions; conditional wrappers, source-row packages, omitted subclaims, weakened/strengthened statements, or broad aggregates must be judged `mismatch` or `uncertain`. Record the model/agent validator metadata and iterate on PaperInterface.lean until the full statement matches. If the dashboard has more than 30 rows, run a no-paper-context LLM audit that checks whether every row is paper-facing; at 120 or more rows, curate the surface before broad human review.

llm_assumption_review.policy: Every paper-facing theorem premise not derived from prior Lean declarations must be declared in Assumptions.lean, listed in assumption_names, and judged by an independent LLM as a true paper/source model assumption rather than a proof assumption.
